main_text.l: ad mortem,
& commoda in morte constitutio. Legitima
praeparatio ad mortem est vniuersalis & particularis. Vniuer-
salis est, qua quis toto vitae suae curriculo ad moriendum
se accingit. Consistit haec praeparatio in tribus hisce parti-
bus. Primo requiritur mortis in vita meditatio, exemplo
Christi. Matth. 16. v. 21. Confer Psal. 39. v. 5. & 90. v. 12.
Oportet autem mortem intueri primo vt poenam peccati
Gen. 1. & 2. deinde vt transitum ex hac vita in vitam aeter-
nam Eccles. 7. v. 1. Luc. 23. v. 43. Secundo requiritur praxis &
instauratio quotidiana poenitentiae, consistens in morti-
ficatione veteris & noui hominis. Ita enim fit, vt vim
roburque mortis, id est, peccatum, quotidie infringamus 1.
Corin. 15. v. 56. & ad primum vitae aeternae gradum in hac
vita accedamus Luc. 17. v. 21. Gal. 2. v. 20, & indies moria-
mur, ne in aeternum moriamur. 1. Cor. 15. v. 31. Pertinet huc
illud elegantissimum Germanorum: Wer da stirbt, ehe er
stirbt, der stirbt nicht wann er stirbt. Neque enim male mori
potest, qui bene vixit. Ita videmus Christi sanctam vitam
praecessisse & peperisse mortem gloriosam. Tertio oportet
res nostras tempestiue constituere. Eccles. 9. v. 10. Gal. 6. v.
10. Sic videmus Christum fideliter fecisse officium suum
praedicando hinc inde euangelium, antequam pateretur,
Praeparatio particularis, siue specialis est, quae fit infirma val-
etudine appetente: vbi officium aegri est triplex. Primum
est erga Deum; operam videl dare reconciliationi sui ipsiu-
s cum Deo in Christo per renouationem fidei & resipi-
scentiae, adeoque confessionem peccati. Psalm. 6. & 38.
Secundum est erga seipsum: vbi aeger curabit animam & cor-
pus. Et animam quidem ita, vt non tam mortem, quam b-
eneficia Dei post mortem intueatur;
vt mortem contem-
pletur non in speculo legis, sed euangelii; denique vt
meditetur prouidentiam Dei, eiusque promissiones, mini-
sterium sanctorum angelorum &c. Corpus vero hac rati-
one, vt omnem valetudini & vitae tuendae atque conser-
uandae det operam, tantisper, dum prorsus a Deo tollatur.
2. Reg. 10. v. 7. Luc. 10. v. 34. Sic autem vtatur medicina,
vt benef[?]

page.notes: The line numbers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 are printed in the left margin; they are placed beside their lines as notes. The paragraph has no clear indent, so it is kept as one paragraph. The first paragraph is marked cont="true" because it begins mid-sentence. The last word of the page is cut off at the foot; the text after "vt benef" is covered by the catchword, so the final word "beneficio" is uncertain and should be checked. The overlay "Vivificatione" in the middle of line 8 is show-through from the other side and is excluded. Long s has been normalised to plain s, including in the German line, where the printed black letter reads "ftirbt" and "ftirbt". The Latin "Ita enim fit" and similar spellings are kept as printed.
